question: Should explicit requester adoption of descendant output count as terminal durable delivery for those descendant runs, even when the requester's final outward send later fails?
rationale: The code can enforce either boundary, but choosing whether internal requester consumption satisfies the product's delivery contract determines retry, failure-marker, cleanup, and persisted-state behavior.

options.title: Accept requester consumption
options.body: Treat exact, identity-matched requester adoption as terminal delivery, after rebase and real restart proof confirm the narrow boundary.

options.title: Require outward delivery
options.body: Keep descendant rows pending until a separately observable delivery succeeds, using requester consumption only as nonterminal provenance.

options.title: Pause this approach
options.body: Close or redesign the branch around the broader durable completion inbox tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/67777.

recommendation.title: Accept requester consumption
recommendation.body: Treat exact, identity-matched requester adoption as terminal delivery, after rebase and real restart proof confirm the narrow boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged descendant-gating work established the closest existing delivery boundary and aggregation contract.
